_note: Curated from public WHO / Government of India material. General information, not medical advice.

bmi_overweight.text: Your BMI is 23 or more. For South Asian adults, health risks start rising at a lower BMI than the global cut-off, so 23 or more counts as overweight. Small, steady changes in diet and activity help.
bmi_overweight.source_title: WHO Expert Consultation. Appropriate body-mass index for Asian populations. The Lancet, 2004

bmi_obese.text: Your BMI is 27.5 or more, which is in the obese range for South Asian adults. A doctor can help you plan safe weight loss.
bmi_obese.source_title: WHO Expert Consultation. Appropriate body-mass index for Asian populations. The Lancet, 2004

physical_activity.text: WHO recommends adults do at least 150 minutes of moderate activity (such as brisk walking) each week. Any activity is better than none.

diet.text: WHO recommends eating at least 400 g (five portions) of fruit and vegetables a day, and limiting salt, sugar and fried foods.

tobacco.text: If you still use tobacco in any form (cigarettes, bidis, gutka or khaini), stopping lowers the risk of heart disease and stroke. A doctor can help you quit.

alcohol.text: Drinking less alcohol lowers health risks. WHO states there is no level of alcohol use that is safe for health.

blood_pressure.text: You said you have been told you have high blood pressure. Keep it under control with your doctor and get it checked regularly.

cholesterol.text: You said you have been told your cholesterol is high. Keep it under control with your doctor; diet and activity also help.

mental_health.text: You reported many days when your mental health was not good. Talking to someone helps. Tele-MANAS, the free national mental health helpline, is available on 14416.
mental_health.source_title: Tele-MANAS, Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, Government of India

regular_checkups.text: Regular check-ups help find conditions like diabetes and high blood pressure early, often before symptoms appear.
